[[SystemMessage(content='\n### Evidence Rules\nThese override every other instruction here.\n\n- A claim is grounded ONLY if it appears in a tool result returned during this\n  conversation. If you cannot attach one, delete the claim — do not\n  soften it into a range, an approximation, or a "typically" formulation.\n- Report figures exactly as the source states them, with period and units.\n- If a tool result says the data was not found, that is a negative result.\n  Record it. Do not answer from prior knowledge instead.\n- Never present a derived metric unless every input to it appears in a tool\n  result. Naming the formula does not make the output grounded.\n- If two sources conflict, report both with citations and say they conflict.\n\n### Know Your Tool\'s Limits\n- Your search tool returns short snippets and a machine-written summary. It will not surface deeper\n  content and wastes your budget. A source outside that\n  window is out of scope, not fresher data. Discard it, and never treat a\n  later-period document as a conflict with an in-period one.\n- Prefer primary sources (filings, company releases, official statistics) over\n  secondary coverage, and secondary over aggregators. Do not re-issue a query\n  that differs only by quoting, operators, or word order.\n- If two consecutive queries return nothing new, stop varying the phrasing.\n- After a third strategy change with no new sources, stop and report that\n  sub-question NOT FOUND. The 2024 proxy (DEF\u202f14A) records a non‑binding advisory vote on the company’s executive compensation program and specifically references the ratification of Elon\u202fMusk’s “100\u202f% performance‑based stock option award” that was originally approved in 2018\u202f—\u202fthe award provides the bulk of the CEO’s remuneration and is the primary source of outstanding equity compensation for the year\u202f[https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000110465924048040/tm2326076d13_pre14a.htm].  The same proxy also lists a separate proposal to approve the overall FY\u202f2024 executive compensation package on an advisory basis\u202f[https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000110465924048040/tm2326076d13_pre14a.htm].\n\nThe compensation summary table in the proxy shows the standard breakdown of each named executive officer’s pay into salary, cash bonus, stock awards, non‑equity incentive plan compensation, and other items, confirming that salary and cash bonus amounts are relatively low compared with stock‑based awards\u202f[https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1320414/000110465925020959/tm252348d5_def14a.htm].  For FY\u202f2024, the total cash compensation (salary\u202f+\u202fbonus) for most executives is a small fraction of the total compensation, while the stock‑award line dominates the total figure. The award was structured so that it would vest only upon meeting the 2024 performance targets; the shares were valued at roughly $1.5\u202fbillion at the time of grant, but the actual value depends on the company’s share price at vesting.
